Given the triangle above, find the length of $\overset{―}{AC}$ rounded to one decimal place.
question.worked_solution:
For an angle $\theta $ in a right triangle, the trigonometric ratios are as follows:

- $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{adjacent leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{adjacent leg}}$

First, note that we are given the length of the adjacent leg $\overset{―}{AB}$ and wish to find the length of the leg $\overset{―}{AC}$ hypotenuse to the given angle $∠A.$

The trigonometric ratio that relates the adjacent leg to the hypotenuse is *cosine*. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(m∠C) & =\frac{\text{adjacent leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡({22}^{∘}) & =\frac{7}{AC} \\ AC\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡({22}^{∘}) & =7 \\ AC & =\frac{7}{\operatorname{cos}⁡({22}^{∘})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using a calculator to evaluate the trigonometric ratio, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =\frac{7}{\operatorname{cos}⁡({22}^{∘})} \\  & =\frac{7}{(0.927\,18…)} \\  & =7.549\,74… \\  & ≈7.5,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.
